'''Karin Anna Reich''' is a German historian of mathematics.

==Career==
From 1967 to 1973 Reich was a scientific assistant at the Research Institute of the [[Deutsches Museum]] in Munich and the Institute for the History of Mathematics and Natural Sciences at [[LMU Munich]], where in 1973, she graduated under supervision of [[Helmuth Gericke]].<ref name="academia-net.org">{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-dr-karin-reich/1134039|title=Prof. Dr. Karin Reich – AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|access-date=2019-01-26|archive-date=21 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190421041118/http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-dr-karin-reich/1134039|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Reich |first1=Karin |title=Die Geschichte der Differentialgeometrie von Gauß bis Riemann (1828–1868) |trans-title=The History of Differential Geometry from Gauss to Riemann (1828–1868) |language=German |journal=Archive for History of Exact Sciences |date=1973 |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=273–376 |doi=10.1007/BF00357392 |s2cid=120832799 }}</ref> In 1980, she completed her time in Munich, publishing ''The development of [[tensor calculus]]'', in 1994 in a revised form as a book.<ref name=hmat.1995.1027>{{cite journal |title=Die Entwicklung des Tensorkalküls. Vom absoluten Differentialkalkül zur Relativitätstheorie |journal=Historia Mathematica |date=1995 |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=323–326 |doi=10.1006/hmat.1995.1027 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1980, she became Professor of the History of Natural Science and Engineering at the [[Stuttgart College of Librarianship]].<ref name=hmat.1995.1027/> In 1980/81 and 1981/82 she had a teaching assignment for the History of Mathematics at [[Heidelberg University]]. In 1981, she represented the Department of History of Science at the [[University of Hamburg]].<ref name=uni-hamburg>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/home/reich/|title=Prof. Dr. Karin Reich (i.R.)|last=Webmaster|first=Dept. Mathematik|date=2012-10-28|website=www.math.uni-hamburg.de|language=de|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref> In 1982, she became associate professor and in 1988 Professor for History of Mathematics at the [[University of Stuttgart]].<ref name="academia-net.org"/> From 1994 until her retirement, she was a professor at the Institute for the History of Natural Science, Mathematics and Engineering at the [[University of Hamburg]], where she succeeded [[Christoph J. Scriba]] as director.<ref name=hmat.1995.1027/>

==Recognition==
Reich is a corresponding member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref name=uni-hamburg/>

==Selected publications==
Reich's publications include biographies of [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]], [[Michael Stifel]] and [[François Viète]].<ref name=hmat.1995.1027/> With Gericke, Reich produced an annotated translation of Viète's ''Analyticam In artem Isagoge'' from 1591.<ref>Review of Gericke and Reich's edition of Viète's work by [[Rosalind Tanner|R. C. H. Tanner]], ''Isis'', 1979, {{JSTOR| 231409}}</ref> She wrote a history of vector-and tensor and differential geometry. With [[Kurt Vogel (historian)|Kurt Vogel]], Gericke and Reich reissued [[Johannes Tropfke]]'s history of elementary mathematics.<ref>Review of Vogel, Gericke, and Reich's edition of Tropfke's work by Michael S. Mahoney, ''Isis'', 1981, {{JSTOR|231202}}</ref>

Reich's books include:
*''Maß, Zahl und Gewicht: Mathematik als Schlüssel zu Weltverständnis und Weltbeherrschung'' [''Measure, number and weight: Mathematics as key to understanding and mastering the world''] (with [[Menso Folkerts]] and [[Eberhard Knobloch]], VCH, Acta Humaniora, Weinheim, 1989)<ref>Review of ''Maß, Zahl und Gewicht'' by [[Walter Purkert]], {{MR|1019830}}; review by U. Lindgren, ''Sudhoffs Archiv'', 1991, {{JSTOR|20777350}}</ref>
*''Die Entwicklung des Tensorkalküls: Vom absoluten Differentialkalkül zur Relativitätstheorie'' [''The development of tensor calculus: From the absolute differential calculus to relativity theory''] (Birkhäuser, 1994)<ref>Review of ''Die Entwicklung des Tensorkalküls'' by [[Detlef Laugwitz]], {{MR|1353442}}; review by [[Clive W. Kilmister|C. W. Kilmister]], ''Isis'', 1997, {{JSTOR|236195}}</ref>
*''Im Umfeld der "Theoria motus": Gauß' Briefwechsel mit Perthes, Laplace, Delambre und Legendre'' [''On matters having to do with the "Theoria motus": Gauss' correspondence with Perthes, Laplace, Delambre and Legendre''] (Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht, 2001)<ref>Review of ''Im Umfeld der "Theoria motus"'' by R. L. Cooke, {{MR|1878353}}</ref>
*''Carl Friedrich Gauß und Russland: Sein Briefwechsel mit in Russland wirkenden Wissenschaftlern'' [''Carl Friedrich Gauss and Russia: His correspondence with scientists working in Russia''] (with Elena Roussanova, De Gruyter, 2012)<ref>Review of ''Carl Friedrich Gauß und Russland'' by [[Ivo Schneider]], {{MR|2896684}}; review by [[Ivor Grattan-Guinness|I. Grattan-Guinness]] ''British Journal for the History of Science'', 2012, {{JSTOR|23275462}}</ref>
*''Carl Friedrich Gauß und Christopher Hansteen: Der Briefwechsel beider Gelehrten im historischen Kontext'' [''Carl Friedrich Gauss and Christopher Hansteen:A correspondence between two scholars in historical context''] (with Elena Roussanova, De Gruyter, 2015)<ref>Review of ''Carl Friedrich Gauß und Christopher Hansteen'' by Thomas Ernst, {{MR|3362733}}</ref>
